page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-256 is a memory-dense virtual machine shape powered by the AMD EPYC 7J13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz, with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing an elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio that provides 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or discrete graphics accelerators, operating with zero GPUs and requiring remote block storage volumes for persistent filesystem needs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned. Without local storage contention or accelerator overhead, the instance maintains a dedicated resource allocation model suited for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity and thread parallelism.

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource profile of the flexible E4 series, offering a balance between multi-threaded EPYC computing capability and high RAM density without the financial overhead of dedicated GPU silicon. Workload fit includes in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, medium-to-large caching tiers, enterprise Java platforms, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
